item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=Can+simulative+reasoning+frameworks+effectively+detect+reasoning+blind+spots+without+relying+on+pre-defined+evaluation+datasets%3F&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7304238\", \"title\": [\"Logical Equivalence, Metacognitive Interference, and Scoring Blind Spots in Inductive Reasoning Tests: On the Structural Invalidity of IQ Scores as a Measure of Reasoning Ability\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The test items used in IQ testing to measure fluid reasoning-whether number series or figural matrix reasoning-all rely on the same inductive reasoning structure: \\\"given finite samples, infer a rule, predict the next term.\\\" This paper identifies three structural problems with such items: (1) Logical equivalence: given any finite sequence or matrix, there often exist multiple generative rules that are computationally equivalent in their outputs, yet the test scores solely on output, making it impossible to distinguish the quality of reasoning paths; (2) Metacognitive interference: high-metacognitive test-takers automatically engage an \\\"auditing procedure\\\" (questioning the premise of the item, identifying multiple interpretations), which consumes working memory resources and induces response delays, resulting in systematic time-pressure penalties; (3) Skeptical disposition and deference to authority presuppositions: the standardized testing procedure implicitly demands that test-takers not question the items themselves, not question the testing institution, and not question the system which claims that intelligence can be measured by a single score. Test-takers with a habitual skeptical disposition automatically initiate the auditing procedure, consuming additional cognitive resources and thereby being systematically penalized in performance. Furthermore, practice effects allow test-takers to compress \\\"reasoning\\\" into \\\"pattern matching,\\\" thereby bypassing the auditing procedure and significantly improving scores-this further demonstrates that when practice becomes normative, what the test measures is no longer fluid reasoning but crystallized pattern recognition. This paper argues that IQ scores are not a pure indicator of \\\"fluid reasoning ability,\\\…

Test-takers with a habitual skeptical disposition automatically initiate the auditing procedure, consuming additional cognitive resources and thereby being systematically penalized in performance. Furthermore, practice effects allow test-takers to compress \\\"reasoning\\\" into \\\"pattern matching,\\\" thereby bypassing the auditing procedure and significantly improving scores-this further demonstrates that when practice becomes normative, what the test measures is no longer fluid reasoning but crystallized pattern recognition. This paper argues that IQ scores are not a pure indicator of \\\"fluid reasoning ability,\\\" but an inseparable hybrid of \\\"fluid reasoning ability,\\\" \\\"familiarity with the test format,\\\" and \\\"deference to authority presuppositions.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7304238\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/1-4020-4943-9_4\", \"title\": [\"Simulative Reasoning and Plan Recognition\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/1-4020-4943-9_4\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1080/13546783.2023.2189163\", \"title\": [\"Bullshit blind spots: the roles of miscalibration and information processing in bullshit detection\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1080/13546783.2023.2189163\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2023, 3, 14]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37201\", \"title\": [\"An Empirical Investigation of Whether Role Asymmetry Can Overcome Reasoning Blind Spots in Homogeneous Models through Adaptive Routing and Local Repair\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Under the test-time compute scaling paradigm, improving the multi-step reasoning accuracy of lightweight large language models within a limited computational budget remains a critical challenge. Existing self-correction and multi-agent debate methods often suffer from rigid interaction schemes, coarse-grained correction, and homogeneous role configurations. Whether role-asymmetric constraints can enable a critic agent to overcome the reasoning biases of its generator has rarely been tested directly. This paper develops a collaborative reasoning framework combining adaptive routing with role-asymmetric local repair, treating this hypothesis as a falsifiable research question, and conducts systematic experiments on two backbone models, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B. Results show that the framework's disadvantage relative to simple baselines is capability-dependent: on the weaker model, it is statistically indistinguishable from standard chain-of-thought and other single-model baselines while significantly outperforming multi-agent debate; on the stronger model, it significantly underperforms most baselines. A sanity check confirms that the critic reliably identifies clearly structured arithmetic errors; however, its recall drops sharply on subtle errors requiring cross-step verification of quantitative relationships, and the net effect of repair mirrors this pattern, close to neutral on the weaker model and clearly negative on the stronger one. Ablation experiments show that the marginal effects of routing and role asymmetry reverse with model capability, turning negative on the stronger model even as removing either component improves its accuracy. These findings provide reproducible empirical evidence for systematic reasoning blind spots in self-criticism by homogeneous models, and indicate that role asymmetry implemented only through prompting cannot reliably overcome cognitive homogeneity.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37201\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 22]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "e3355155b59a711f233000bca6611e86418c165907d11e5e5142093f02d85979", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unrecognized_reasoning_limits", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.7304238", "doi:10.1007/1-4020-4943-9_4", "doi:10.1080/13546783.2023.2189163", "doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37201"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7304238", "https://doi.org/10.1007/1-4020-4943-9_4", "https://doi.org/10.1080/13546783.2023.2189163", "https://doi.org/10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37201"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
